utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Case number IT-95-9-T, the Prosecutor versus Blagoje Simic, Miroslav Tadic, and Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Pantelic, you're continuing with your examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I just wonder whether we should address the Court with the -- with regard to the issue which was raised by the Prosecution yesterday and after the consultations of our --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Can --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Our clients.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Can you just complete your questions and then we will deal with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You mean after the set of questions for examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. As I indicated yesterday, it won't be closed until we deal with the matter which was raised by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: That was my misunderstanding. I thought you were -- instructed us only for the yesterday's session of examination-in-chief. But I will proceed. Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: BLAGOJE SIMIC [Resumed]

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Pantelic: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, doctor.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday I analysed additionally these exhibits, so now we will turn back to a document that was discussed during the testimony of Stevan Todorovic, and I would like to clarify a technical matter, translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Exhibit P77. Yes. You may put the English version on the ELMO because it's an issue of translation, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please read out the heading of your document in the upper left corner.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "Assembly of the Serb people of Bosanski Samac Municipality and Pelagicevo under formation," and then under that it says, "The Municipal Crisis Staff." And then underneath we have number 02-10/92. And then date, 17th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since this is an order that you already talked about yesterday, tell me, please, pursuant to this order, was -- were the weapons brought to the Municipal Crisis Staff ever confiscated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where the confiscated weapons were stored? Do you have any knowledge of that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In military and police locations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, maybe it's a question of translation; maybe not. You asked Dr. Simic were -- this is line 19, line 20/21: "Were the weapons brought to the Municipal Crisis Staff ever confiscated?" And Dr. Simic's answer is no. And then your question is: "Do you know where the confiscated weapons were stored?" Well, he said they weren't confiscated, so how could confiscated weapons therefore be stored? There seems to be some inconsistency there. Maybe you could clarify, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. I believe that's the translation. I will clarify that. Thank you for your intervention, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me repeat the question: Were confiscated weapons ever brought into the premises of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: But again, just as a matter of clarification, but weapons were confiscated, were they or were they not?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were weapons confiscated? And if so, where were they stored and whose responsibility was this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: According to information that I have, it was stored in military and police locations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday we took a look at the document P58 before we stopped working -- P98.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... P98.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You can put the Serbian version on the ELMO so that other co-accused can follow it. Are you familiar with this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this document discussed at the session of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who authored this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The staff, professional staff of the municipal assembly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the purpose of this document, of this memo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was an appeal for assistance to be provided to the Serbs imprisoned in the municipality of Odzak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next document also has to do with --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Could -- could on the ELMO we see the signature on the bottom, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Did you sign this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. P99.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The same question: Are you familiar with this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who is the author of this document? Who prepared it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The professional staff of the municipal assembly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this your signature here on this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It looks like it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember discussing this document, this issue with other members of the Crisis Staff at your sessions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will now just give you the gist of this document, but does this also have to do with an appeal addressed to the executive council?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. We called this a cry for help to be provided to the imprisoned Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this refers to the Serbs imprisoned in the territory of Odzak municipality.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: The addressee of the document may be important for you. Mr. Pantelic said that it was -- it was addressed to the executive council. You might like to know what executive council. Are we talking about the Bosanski Samac executive council or something else. Also, at the top of the document -- oh, I'm sorry. My apologies. Yes. It speaks for itself. I withdraw my objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Usher. Now could we have, please, P100.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yesterday we already touched upon the relations with SAO Semberija and Majevica. Now, tell me please, do you remember this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Although this document is self-explanatory, can you confirm that this has to do with the joining of SAO Semberija and Majevica and the harmonisation of regulations, of Samac municipality with those of SAO Semberija and Majevica.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this your signature down at the bottom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It looks like my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Usher. Now I would like to have Exhibit P101, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: The last two answers with respect to signature by Dr. Simic are "it looks like my signature." Does he remember actually -- if he remembers the document, he remembers the discussions re the document, can he answer more directly than "it looks like my signature"?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember signing this document at the time when it was drafted?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. But I have a copy in front of me, not the original.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So now we have 101; yes? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a document that also speaks about the relations between the Serb Municipality of Samac and SAO Semberija and Majevica. It was issued on the same date, and it says that you had certain representatives representing the Municipality of Bosanski Samac in SAO Semberija and Majevica; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since this took place on the same date, was this also discussed at the session of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember signing this signature?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The original, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Signing this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The original, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does this seem to you like it could be your signature?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It resembles my signature.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Correction of interpreter: The representative of the Samac Municipality in SAO Semberija and Majevica was in fact Dr. Simic itself. This is what the document says.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now could we have Exhibit P102, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you remember this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who drafted this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The executive council of the municipal assembly, namely, Secretariat for Economy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the justification of the relevant organ of the municipality when the draft of this decision was presented to the Crisis Staff to be adopted, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The justification was that the municipality had no revenue and it didn't levy any taxes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that was the reason for adopting this decision, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that the municipality would have a source of revenue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please take a look at the signature on the last page. Do you remember signing this document on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the original.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Usher. Could we have P103, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, this is a decision that deals with certain territorial delineation between the municipalities of Modrica and Brod. Can you tell us, if you remember, what the circumstances were under which this decision was adopted, and please tell us, do you remember why was this decision discussed at the Crisis Staff sessions, if it was discussed at all and adopted -- or rather, the War Presidency.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This decision has to do with territorial demarcation between these municipalities because between these two municipalities there was another municipality that had a completely different governing body. It was governed by military authorities. And we couldn't --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: He was talking about three municipalities and here in the transcript I see two municipalities. Actually, it was the municipality of Bosanski Samac, Modrica, and the third was Brod. And here in the transcript it says two municipalities. So it will make a confusion. I didn't want to interrupt Mr. Simic while giving his testimony, but I had to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we have clarification.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So let's continue. You spoke about demarcation between three municipalities, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please continue, Dr. Simic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Due to the presence of military administration, military rule in the territory of Odzak municipality, we couldn't define the borders of any of these municipalities, and therefore we couldn't define jurisdiction itself. And all of this represented a problem in the operation of state companies that had their seats mostly in Doboj and branch offices in Samac, Modrica, Odzak, and Brod. This commission was established in order to try and get the talks going with other municipalities as well as representatives of the military administration in order to one day abolish the military rule, and there was several proposals that were presented to the People's Assembly of Republika Srpska, and sometime in the middle of 1993 the People's Assembly of Republika Srpska adopted a law on abolishing the military rule in Odzak and establishing the Municipality of Odzak with civilian government. This law also defined clearly borders between municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Now can we have P105, please. Sorry. Could we have Exhibit P105.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Look at the last page and see the date of the document. When was this document done?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the 15th of December, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at that time you were what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was president of the Assembly of the Samac Municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This document follows up on the previous presentation. Tell us, when you submitted this bill to the People's Assembly of the Republika Srpska, was this bill adopted? Did it become a law?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. This bill was rejected and the People's Assembly took a different decision. I mean, all of the proposals that came from the ground were rejected and they passed their own decision, which was to rescind military rule and introduce civilian administration in the Municipality of Odzak and that the Municipality of Odzak should have its pre-war boundaries.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you look at the last page of this letter, please, under item 1 in annexes, we see the report of the Deputy Commander of the 1st Krajina Corps for civilian matters, for civilian affairs. So, on page 3, look at the third -- look, please, at page 3, doctor, the annexes. What was the role of the military element, that is, the assistant commander of the 1st Krajina commander for civilian affairs and what was the role of the military bodies in the resolution of the situation. Briefly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, they also submitted their own proposal to the People's Assembly. They had a proposal of their own.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Usher. Could we have now Exhibit P106, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This document speaks for itself, so it is a decision to abolish Crisis Staff in neighbourhood communities in the municipality territory. Is this your signature here on this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I know that you are not a graphologist, but could you tell us whose signature is it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, it doesn't look like my signature and I don't know whose signature it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. My next question is: Do you remember if the Crisis Staff discussed this decision?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And whose suggestion was it? Whose proposal was it to abolish it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was the military who made such a proposal to the Ministry of Defence and the Ministry of Defence then forwarded it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you please look at Article 3 of the decision and comment on it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "The Crisis Staff of the municipality" --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't have to read it aloud. You can read it to yourself and then comment on it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were endeavouring to preserve the civilian authority neighbourhood communities too, but the problem arose with the people. The Ministry of Defence and the military would not tolerate any longer ten or more people sitting in those staffs and dodging their military obligation, so they demanded that it be brought down to one or two people and if possible that they be pensioners or disabled or something. And at that stage we thought about representatives in neighbourhood communities and these decisions were being prepared.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In other words, this was an effort invested by the Crisis Staff, an attempt to cut down on the municipal administration; is that what it meant?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Usher. Could we have Exhibit P107, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Are you familiar with this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In point of fact, it is a document which follows up on your previous explanation. These are representatives of the Crisis Staff in neighbourhood communities; is that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And now, will you please comment briefly on Article 3 of this decision.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The representative now had to settle all the problems concerning civilian affairs in the territory of neighbourhood communities by himself according to this and, of course, seeking previously the consent of the Crisis Staff of the municipality and the executive council.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, that you mention the neighbourhood community, the local community, I think it would be very important for this case and for the Chamber to know if the territory of a neighbourhood or local community was perhaps synonymous with a village, for instance, in the territory of Bosanski Samac, would you say that that's what it was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, as a rule.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Can we have P108, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a decision of the War Presidency to change the name of the town and municipality of Bosanski Samac. Do you remember this decision?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So there was a discussion about it and then the War Presidency took this decision on the 2nd of October, 1992; is that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And whose proposal was it? Who drafted this decision?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The professional services of the executive council.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember what was the reason behind this decision? Do you remember perhaps some of the interventions during the discussion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, one of the reasons is that earlier Samac used to be called Samac, and another reason was that at that time there were already three municipalities which were called Samac, so the Serb Municipality of Bosanski Samac, the Croat Municipality of Bosanski Samac, Domaljevac on the Croat side -- on the Croatian side, Slavonski Samac, and it all made the situation complicated. It was difficult to tell these different municipalities apart on the radio and so on and so forth. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, Mr. Pantelic asked two questions: Whose proposal it was and who drafted the decision. We found out who drafted the decision, but we haven't found out who proposed it. It was asked, so perhaps the witness ought to answer that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Can we have the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. I believe that that was the second part of the explanation -- that will be the second part of the explanation of Dr. Simic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Answer the question, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The proposal originated with the executive council of the municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the War Presidency ever discuss discrimination against non-Serb ethnicities when discussing the decision? Did somebody say, for instance, "Now we would call ourselves Samac against the interests of Muslims or Croats"? Were there any such interventions in the discussion that was conducted?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, there were never any such interventions. And had anyone aspired to this, then we would have called it the Serb Samac. But we did not want it to have any prefix. We wanted everybody to live in Samac only and that is why it is called Samac, without emphasising the ethnic aspect.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in 1995 how was the municipality of Samac divided, that is, the territory of Samac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was split into the Croat Samac, Domaljevac, and the Serb municipality of Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the former -- that is, part of the former Bosanski Samac municipality called Prud, who did that go to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That part of the former municipality of Bosanski Samac went to the third municipality, Odzak, that is. So at the former municipality of Bosanski Samac before the war was after the war split into three municipalities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the armed conflict, did this Croat municipality of Bosanski Samac, Domaljevac, exist ever, or was that territory ever in the hands of the Serb authorities?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That territory was never in the hands of the Serb authorities, and the front line along the boundary of these two municipalities never shifted during the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Usher. Could we have, please, Exhibit P109.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Will you comment on this decision. Does this decision refer to your appointment as the president of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us, does it reflect the factual situation, the date that we have up there, is that the date when it was adopted?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The decision was taken on the 19th of April, but the professional service typed it on the 17th in order to ensure the continuity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you sign it on behalf of the Crisis Staff? Do you recognise your signature?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah. I did sign the original.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Usher. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, I don't know if the Chamber is having the same difficulty, but I have trouble understanding the meaning of "ensuring the continuity." I wonder what it mean that is a document has to be backdated in order to ensure continuity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yeah. MR. DI FAZIO: It doesn't mean anything to me. I wonder if you are having the same trouble. If you are, it might be good to clarify it now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Because it -- the assumptions have to be cleared.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Explain the reason for this continuity that you just mentioned. What do you think and what knowledge do you have about it? Why was this decision pre-dated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I am perplexed too. Legal people try to explain it to me, but the clearest explanation that I have received so far was that that provided for the seniority, for the number of years in service.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Usher. Please, could we have Exhibit P110.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This document speaks for itself, so only a couple of comments. So it was so this disposition or this decision was adopted on the 30th of May, 1992, and it say that is Milan Simic is appointed president of the executive council of the Municipality of Bosanski Samac; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in relation to this appointment, were there any disagreements in the Crisis Staff? Because there were two candidates and there was a certain procedure. There was some lobbying for Milan Simic. You explained it to us yesterday.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Usher. And now could we have Exhibit P111.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This document speaks for itself too. Mr. Mirko Lukic appointed the deputy president or vice-president, was he that other person that you mentioned who ran in these elections against Milan Simic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Could we have Exhibit P112, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Are you familiar with this decision of the 30th of May, 1992 to set up the executive council and other administrative agencies?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who drafted this decision? Who is the author?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Administrative bodies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that the Crisis Staff practically only discussed it and adopted something that was prepared in advance; is that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me. Dr. Simic, if I hear you correctly, the Crisis Staff, based on your answer to Mr. Pantelic's question -- the Crisis Staff simply signed an already-prepared document. Is it usual that -- was it the usual practice in Samac to have bureaucrats, functionaries, prepare on their own -- on their own a document and then Crisis Staff would simply look at it, discuss it, and sign it, or were there discussions with one of the civil servants present taking notes and the discussions were then put into draft form, written form, which was then brought back to the Crisis Staff for the Crisis Staff to review and adopt and sign?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This kind of paper, like all other papers, at first are proposed by way of a draft, and that's what they are called, a draft. The proposal is made by administrative bodies, and this can only be written by legal people. During those days the Crisis Staff was already abolished, and later there was this War Presidency and also there was the municipal parliament, and then they would explain their proposal there. Then the members of the legislative part of the executive -- I mean, no, the legislative government of the municipal assembly, they would discuss it. Then there would be a vote, either a public vote or by secret ballot. And if there is a majority vote, if over half of those present are in favour of, then the decision is typed out. It is no longer called a draft. It is the final text. If there were any amendments during the discussion, then these amendments are discussed and then these amendments are included in the final text, which is then brought for signature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Usher. Could we have exhibit, please, P116, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please take look at this document and tell me, are you familiar with this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am familiar with it from the records, the documents of this court -- I mean, its contents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall having signed this document on the 14th of December, 1992, at the premises of the heating plant where the seat of the War Presidency was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did sign a similar record. I don't know whether this is the original.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were representatives of the military court from Banja Luka there? Specifically, was the investigating judge there and the military prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, although of course you're not a legal expert, but in these proceedings before a military court - and if you know, in other proceedings before other relevant courts - is a record compiled like here at this Tribunal, where every word is recorded, or does the person who is carrying out the examination, like the investigating judge, does that person then dictate what the person who was giving the answers said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The difference is that then we had a normal conversation, and then one of the prosecutors would make a summary, dictate this to the typist, and thus create this record.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So he conveyed the content of your statement, not faithfully, word for word, but in abbreviated form, abridged form.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In abridged form.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, towards the end of this record, it says that there is a note that you heard the dictation and that therefore practically you have no objections. Were you aware of that fact then? Were you cautioned then? Did the judiciary authority caution you about this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was not cautioned. I was not told that this was any kind of court document. Furthermore, I did not read that paper, and I can say that all of this was done in a high-pressure atmosphere.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In this document on page 3 - I think it's underlined as well - in paragraph 2 there is a sentence. It says that "Crni comes for the second time at the invitation of the War Presidency of Samac." Is that correct, this statement included in this court record?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Stevan Todorovic claimed that the War Presidency had invited Crni. However, when preparing myself for the defence, for my defence before this court, I did not find any such decision in the documents of the War Presidency, nor does anybody know about this. When I gave additional thought to this, I didn't find it logical because Crni was an inhabitant of Samac. He lived in Samac. He was married to a woman from Samac. He had a family in Samac. He had a child in Samac. And it wasn't logical to me at all that he should be invited if he lived there had anyway.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But he was arrested first and then expelled to Serbia. Do you know about him having come back in the meantime?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He had been arrested, expelled to Serbia, demobilised, and then as a civilian he came to Samac to see his family.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As for volunteers from Serbia, did you ever offer them financial compensation for their engagement in carrying out combat operations in the territory of the municipality of Samac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, I don't think the witness has answered the previous question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: Mr. Pantelic asked the witness in relation to the phrase "Crni comes for the second time at the invitation of the War Presidency of Samac," and the witness went on to describe why that would not be logical. But he hasn't actually said if he told the court that. That was the question, and we should know whether or not he made that statement, that utterance, that is contained in this document to the court.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When they took that statement, there were other members of the War Presidency there. Stevan Todorovic was also sitting there. He's the one who brought them, because they did not know where I was. While they were talking to me, they were talking to Todorovic as well, and they made a summary on that basis and they typed what they typed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who were the other members of the War Presidency who were there then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think Savo Popovic was present.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please look at the penultimate paragraph on page 3 of this decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, has your question been answered? Because you asked specifically whether or not the accused did make that statement. MR. DI FAZIO: Well, actually, on reflection, no, it hasn't. I rather gathered that there's a suggestion inherent in that answer that maybe the words are those of Todorovic. I don't know. But --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Can we have a specific answer. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. You are quite right, and I omitted to notice that there hadn't been a direct question to that very simple -- sorry, a direct answer to that very simple question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In relation to Crni, could you just say whether you stated this on the 14th of December, 1992 before the investigating judge of the military court in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Take a look at --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Pantelic. Dr. Simic, did you sign -- did you sign this statement, this typed abridged summary of what went on in that room?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat his answer. The interpreters could not understand what he said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can you repeat your answer. The interpreters didn't catch it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At the end of this document, where it says that this document -- this statement was not read out to me, that's where I signed this record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The penultimate paragraph on page 3 of this document. It's a poor copy, but take a look at it. It says here that you had been in the office or at the position of the presidency of the War Presidency from April 1991.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At that time there was no War Presidency yet or was there a Crisis Staff in 1991.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that is a mistake in the record, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: If you -- I'm sorry. It's an important document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: I don't want to interrupt the flow of the examination of my learned friend. I'll try to keep my interjections to a minimum, but it is important. The witness said that the statement -- he signed the statement, the statement that was not read out to him. On the English translation that I've got, it says that he doesn't wish to read the record, since the statement was dictated out loud. That seems to be in -- a degree of inconsistency. It may not have been read out to him but it may have been dictated out loud. There's a difference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Maybe you can read the document in Serbo-Croat, then the interpreters -- MR. DI FAZIO: That's a good idea. And then perhaps I'll invite Mr. Pantelic to ask him if what's contained there in that last paragraph after he's read it out is true or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Your Honour. I agree.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please slowly read the penultimate paragraph of this document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "I have been in the position of the president of the War Presidency since April 1991."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Pantelic. I think what we want is the paragraph to be read out concerning the dictated -- the dictation of the statement and so on, not the sentence concerning 1991. So what we want is the sentence following that, just before the signatures.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please read the paragraph underneath the one you've just read out.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "I have nothing more to state, and I do not wish to read the record because my statement was dictated out loud and, as such, I sign it without any objections."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Under which conditions was this statement taken? Because we see that it was not in the court itself but it was in the field. What was the atmosphere like when this statement was being taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The atmosphere was the following: Two prosecutors were present, one typist, military security personnel. The previous days there were arrests of civilian authorities of the municipality of Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you feel that you were under pressure when you were giving this statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Absolutely, yes, because I did not know whether I would be arrested or not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you concentrated, focussed when you gave this statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have legal counsel, legal assistance?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you describe those times to us and the relationship between the military and the civilian authorities. What was going on? Because we can see that this is the month of December 1992. Were there any tensions, if I can put it that way, between certain military circles and the civilian authorities precisely at that time?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, don't -- don't give evidence. Let -- ask the witness what was the atmosphere, what was going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: It is the accused who was there and he is the one who should give evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is precisely the period when the conflict culminated between the civilian authorities and the military authorities, especially in that area. Later on this conflict was deepened in all other areas. There were some events at that time, such as the closing of the corridor, the killing of scouts, arrests of security officials of brigades, then the arrival of volunteers, a major concentration of brigades of the Army of Republika Srpska in an exceptionally small area, which led to incidents every day. And this resulted in mutual interference, especially of the military authorities that had force in their hands in the affairs of the civilian authorities. There was even a tendency to have the civilian authorities wither away altogether.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have the impression that the proceedings between the military judiciary was rigged in a way?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I object to that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: A very leading question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I've warned you before that -- don't give evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I will just rephrase my question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please tell me, Dr. Simic: In view of what you have just told us, what was your personal impression? Do you have any additional knowledge concerning the nature of the proceedings that took place before the military court in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't comment on that because I was not present at the trial, nor was I there in that court, nor was I ever called to testify before that court, nor was I ever told that a record had been taken based on my statement that would eventually be used as a court exhibit. I wasn't even summoned by the first instance military court in Bijeljina, when they convicted me, nor was I summoned by the higher court in Han Pijesak, which reviewed this judgment later on; therefore, I was never summoned to appear as a witness in court. And as far as I know, nobody went to testify from the Samac municipality area.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Just a correction in the transcript. It's page 26, line 22. Instead of "military court in Bijeljina," we heard that he made a reference to military court in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: I just have one last question on this document. Page 26, lines 20 to 23. Dr. Simic, you say that you were never told that a record had been taken based on your statement that would eventually be used as a court exhibit. I'm afraid I am a little bit lost on that because you knew that this record, shall we say, of what you were saying had been dictated, and you signed it. So are you talking about something different in your answer where you say you were never told that a record had been taken? Perhaps you could just clarify that last point for me.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That I was told that -- had I been told that my statement would later be used in court, I would engage counsel, because I wouldn't agree to give any statements that would be later used in court without legal advice. And I didn't know -- or I would expect to be summoned to testify in court based on the statement. It is very hard to summarise something that has been said over one hour in one typed page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And another question that may be useful in order to clarify this: You were at that stage examined by the investigative judge, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: An investigative judge of the military court.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, we shall turn to some other matters that stem from previous statements of witnesses and previous documents. Please tell me, what do you personally know about the conditions and reasons for a transfer of some residents of Samac into Zasavica? What do you know about Zasavica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What I know about Zasavica differs greatly from the information I acquired in these proceedings. The information we had at the time were such that civilian police stationed at one entrance into Zasavica - and that is a local commune with a large territory that has at least four to five entry/exit points and borders with the Bosna River, which is very shallow in summertime - so the purpose was to have civilian police placed -- two policemen at the entry point into Zasavica in order to protect the operation of farms in that local commune which continued operating even in the state of war and imminent threat of war and provided food for the army and civilian residents of Samac and public kitchens there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. I have to interrupt you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: For the benefit of my learned friends, our internal number of this document which I would like to introduce at this stage is KS2/1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now that you've mentioned this topic concerning the operation of farms, please tell us, did you sign this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember that this issue was discussed at the sessions of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Generally speaking, we spoke about activating farms. However, these were operative matters that the executive council was in charge of, in fact. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, again, I seek a further clarification because I gather that Mr. Pantelic is leaving the topic of the placing of policemen at Zasavica. I understood the witness to be saying that civilian police were placed at various checkpoints -- entry points -- I'm sorry -- entry points around Zasavica in order to continue to protect the operation of the farms because of the state of war and imminent threat of war. I don't understand if policemen placed at various checkpoints were to protect against military incursion by enemy forces or whether they were there to just provide general police security because of the general troubled times. They're two distinct and different things, and I'm not quite clear from the answer and it might be important for the Chamber to know whether these are protecting against military incursion or general troubles at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We will come back later to this document, but let's clarify this first. What you know about that police checkpoint in Zasavica, do you know what was the nature and purpose of that police checkpoint there? Can you explain that to the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why was a checkpoint placed in Zasavica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said that there was just one checkpoint in Zasavica, only on one entry point. Therefore, not on all entry points but only on one. Zasavica has four to five entry or exit points and a large territory and in order to protect a village of that size, one would need at least 100 people. Those two policemen, based on the information that we received, were tasked with guarding the farms, which were actively operating, and this is one of the documents speaking about how the food was provided for those farms. When we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The -- the Prosecutor did ask was it to protect generally, general police work, or was it to protect the farms against army incursions of the enemy forces.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They were there to protect farms, mostly from local residents, not from the enemy.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean in order to prevent looting of the farms by individuals.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in order to prevent individuals from looting the farm. But I also wanted to say why were the farms activated in that village as well. Because that was the only village in Samac municipality that wasn't shelled. That village was not shelled by enemy forces. We never ever received an information saying that a single shell landed in that village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, please take a look at this document and give us your comments. Please explain to the Trial Chamber what was the purpose of this decision and tell us how this mechanism performed. First of all, tell us when was this decision passed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the 13th of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please now explain this document to us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then and in other times the farms brought in food from the central silo. The central silo is where the food was stored and mixed and so-called food mix was produced to feed the cattle, and that process of maintaining the farms and feeding the cattle was used in the same way as before. The food was taken in the agricultural concern and then the food was brought in to feed the cattle and they continued producing eggs and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And once they received the feed for cattle and chicken and so on, how did the farm pay back to the agricultural concern for the feed? Would they pay them back in money or in goods?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They would pay them back in goods, in meat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, please tell me, we see the names of two farmers here in this document who on the 13th of May, 1992 were approved 3 tonnes of cattle feed. Tell us, please, this gentleman here, Senjic Juro, what was his ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He's a Croat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Therefore, the Crisis Staff -- and you can correct me if I'm wrong -- the Serb Crisis Staff on the 13th of June -- 13th of May, 1992 delivered 3 tonnes of cattle feed to Senjic Juro, a Croat from Zasavica, whereas he took on an obligation to return the value of that to PIK Samac upon the completion of that process; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did farmers in such a process make certain profit upon paying back the value of the feed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. They would have some goods left over, some meat.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to tender this document into evidence, Your Honour, please, if there's no objections, of course. MR. DI FAZIO: No objection, if Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Can we have the numbers, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be D71/1 and D71/1 ter, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The next document is also related to this process, and I will very briefly pass -- go through this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is this your signature on this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So somebody dealt with these matters on behalf of the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The executive council of the municipal assembly, Secretariat for Agriculture.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But they used the name of the Crisis Staff, and you don't know for what reason.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat the answer. The interpreters didn't hear it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can you repeat the answer, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the answer. The interpreters didn't hear you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the time no other stamp existed, a stamp of a different form.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please be more precise. You said that there were three stamps of the Serb municipality. Please complete your answer. What stamp was missing or lacking?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They didn't have a stamp with a different form. This stamp was manufactured in three versions or three --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's simplify this. Was there no stamp then bearing the text of the executive council of the municipal assembly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it didn't exist then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please take a look at the date on this document. Tell us what the date is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 13th of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the ethnicity of the owner of the farm called Tunjic Mato?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A Croat.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... If there is no objections, Your Honour. And it's about time for our break. MR. DI FAZIO: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we have the number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. It will be D72/1 and D72/1 ter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, how many more minutes? You were supposed to end up yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, frankly, I have only one document, which is basically the same issue. And then -- then I will quite efficiently go through, let's say, maybe 20 questions with regard to the statements of the OTP witnesses. Here we have to clarify certain events and facts. And I don't believe that Dr. Simic will give an expanded version of answers. Maybe just yes or no. So in total maybe, let's say, half an hour maybe, 40 minutes, something like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I will finish then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We'll adjourn and continue our proceedings at 11.30 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic, you're continuing.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour. I have one more document to discuss. Basically it's the same issue. For the benefit of our friends from the Prosecution, it's KC2/3.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Dr. Simic, is the date on this document the 18th of May, 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise the signature on this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It looks like mine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what is this document about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Agricultural Company Samac is authorised to issue feed concentrate G-12 for heifers and the total amount of feed is 8 tonne, metric tonnes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you perhaps know what is the ethnicity of the owner of the farm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Croat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The English translation shows the date as 18th August. Is that a mistake? Because you said the witness said the date is 18th May, 1992. Which is the correct date?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, you are right. Your Honour, maybe we could put the B/C/S version on the ELMO and then our friends from technical booth can zoom onto the date, because it is handwritten document, the left top side. And maybe ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: What does it look like to you -- or the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you tell us, what do you think? Is it August or May?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is May 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And in any case, the accused knows about the document. So we take May -- 18th May 1992 as a correct date.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: There's no objection, I take it, from the Prosecution to this production?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: There's no objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we have the numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be D73/1 and D73/1 ter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since we are on this topic about Zasavica, tell us, did you have any personal knowledge whether in Zasavica there were also the inhabitants of some villages from the neighbourhood of Samac who had to be relocated from the villages, and do you know why, if that is so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not at that time. Depends on the period of time that we are talking about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm talking about May 1992.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had no such information.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you said that you had information about some other period of time. Will you explain it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, that other period, when I returned from my sick leave -- so I was absent for several months, and then I was informed that there were certain happenings in Zasavica. They were in part presented here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happenings do you mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, that in Zasavica there were Serbs and Muslims and Croats.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who did you hear that from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From Stevan Todorovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did he explain to you? Why was that done?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is very -- it was very difficult to understand his answers and the words he used. But as far as I could understand, he had transferred some of the civilian population from Samac to Zasavica because members of those families had swum across the Sava and were divulging information about the shelling of the town of Samac and the aftermath of those shellings, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me. Dr. Simic, you say that it was very difficult to understand Stevan Todorovic's answers and the words he used. Why was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because he was under the influence of alcohol day in, day out. And one could say that it was a very high degree of intoxication. He also used all sorts of pills, and one could never know what particular mood he was in. And the span of his reactions was from the high tension to high emotions. Sometimes he reacted like a child, so that his reality seemed to us very questionable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Dr. Simic, as a highly educated person and having got a degree as a doctor, you have also sworn the oath of Hippocrates, haven't you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No audible response]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Isn't what you are talking about and telling us about Mr. Todorovic, isn't -- aren't you breaking your oath?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. It would be breaking the oath if he were my patient. But I am not accused because -- I didn't understand. I did not understand what you just said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Well, you were a co-accused, and do you think that this is, so to say, freeing you from the oath you have given as a doctor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not treat Stevan Todorovic. He was not my patient, and therefore I am under no professional obligation towards him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: You said three days ago --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the Judge, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The microphone is still switched off.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: You said three days ago that he was your patient; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Stevan Todorovic before the war at times would run into the emergency service, where I was on duty, and ask me for a prescription. But I cannot consider myself his doctor, because I did not have his file. I did not examine him. I didn't establish a diagnosis. And he was not filed as my patient. So I merely knew from his reactions when he came to me to write for him a prescription for him or for his mother or for his father or whoever.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Your explanation today doesn't confirm what you said three days ago when you said that Stevan Todorovic was a patient of yours. Can you recall that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've just explained it, what were my professional contacts with him. I never examined him, therefore -- he never undressed in front of me so that I could listen to him. He would always run in. He would jump the queue. He never waited for queues, especially when we were on duty, so that he could be issued with a prescription in order for him to obtain a medicine. And that is the amount of my professional contact with him. This was my political observation, and since this is a criminal court, I have to defend myself and I have to explain what my impressions were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: And if I may continue, you feel free to reveal whatever about Stevan Todorovic, not present here, sitting in a Spanish prison?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Before you answer that, Dr. Simic, I appreciate that what you were saying was in response to my question concerning why you couldn't understand his words, and I also understand that you are under an obligation to tell the truth pursuant to the solemn declaration here. So you were responding to my question. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment. I haven't answered. I haven't answered Judge Lindholm. Judge Lindholm asked me if I thought that I had the right, and I do not know whether I can answer that question. I need some legal advice on that. I mean, with regard to the Hippocrates oath.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I think after Judge Williams's intervention, the matter is left at that. So we'll proceed with the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But did you hear from another source about the reasons for this, as you told us, police operation in relation to Zasavica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All stories circulated around. At this point I cannot really pinpoint the source of those stories. But when the chief of police performed his duties, we simply thought that he was the one whose duty it was to provide the information.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you personally have any knowledge about cases of mistreatment of civilians who were temporarily placed in Zasavica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Stevan Todorovic in his capacity of the chief of police -- I mean, you personally, did he ever report to you about possible incidents that might have taken place in Zasavica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any personal knowledge about the living and housing conditions in Zasavica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any barbed wire around Zasavica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Zasavica mentioned as a camp in Samac at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Stevan Todorovic report to you - I mean to you personally - about the existence of prisons, several detention units, if I may call them that, in Samac?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We could not hear the witness's answer because the witness speaks over the counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can the witness -- can you repeat the answer? The interpreters didn't get it. And perhaps you should move closer to the microphones.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, not to me personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But did he report to the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, now and then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That there was a certain number of arrested individuals in prison in Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he report to the Crisis Staff about the grounds for the arrest of those civilians?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Insofar as one could infer from his reports, because he had difficulties concentrating on a particular topic, one was led to conclusion that those were Islamic terrorists, according to him, and that he had enough evidence to file a criminal report against them and request an investigation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Within that context, did he also mention Croat civilians?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you personally know about the incidents committed by Stevan Todorovic in Samac in those detention units?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Stevan Todorovic attend the meetings of the Crisis Staff and speak about crimes and offences he had committed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you learn from some other sources what Stevan Todorovic was doing at that time in Samac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you support the appointment of Stevan Todorovic as vice-president of the executive council of the Municipality of Samac in 1995?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Within the civilian authorities in Samac, was some kind of initiative launched to investigate the abuses of Stevan Todorovic by a commission of the Ministry of the Interior of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any other efforts to inform the appropriate police authorities about the behaviour of Stevan Todorovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In what sense? Could you explain this.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We spoke to his chief in Doboj, Andrija Bjelosevic, and also with every member of the Ministry of the Interior who came to that area. And we drew their attention to the fact that we believed that Stevan Todorovic does not know how to do that job and that he should be replaced.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Perhaps at this stage in the examination-in-chief Dr. Simic could clarify what he means by civilian authorities in Samac, firstly, and secondly who the "we" is who spoke to the chief in Doboj. It may be of assistance to the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well. I'm sure the accused has heard that. He can explain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me. And also, Dr. Simic, as well perhaps you could give us the timing. There's no mention of the year when these efforts were being made.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We intensified these efforts towards the end of 1992, in terms of informing the Ministry of the Interior that a initiative should be launched for Stevan Todorovic to be replaced. The Ministry of the Interior sent a commission which spent some time towards the end of 1992 and beginning of 1993 in Samac and it investigated the work of Stevan Todorovic as well as of other authorities in the Public Security Station. In addition to that, one of the high officials of the Ministry of the Interior at that time - I think it was the assistant minister for the public sector - advised Stevan Todorovic to tender a resignation on his own and to withdraw from that position. Tomo Kovac was the name of this high official. Stevan Todorovic talked everywhere about this intervention, about the intervention of this MUP official. He made fun of his proposal, and he said that it didn't cross his mind ever to resign from that position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And the other point of clarification was when you answered that we spoke to his chief, meaning the chief of Todorovic. What -- who do you mean by "we"? Yourself and who -- or was it yourself as the Crisis Staff or the War Presidency?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At that time the assembly had already started to function, so this was a delegation on behalf of the municipal assembly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before the assembly started to work, that is to say, in the period from April 1992 until the end of 1992, were there any efforts made by you personally or --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Officials from the Ministry of the Interior were contacted then, and this was discussed with them when they came to the territory of the municipality. We asked them to deal with this problem because in Samac this was not a good thing. Tomo Kovac conducted that conversation then and advised Todorovic to resign on his own. Todorovic said this to almost everyone he would see.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Again, same point of clarification. Your Honour, Dr. Simic has several times within the last few moments used the words "we." It is entirely unclear as to whether he's including himself there or whether it's a generic "we" meaning the municipality. I'd ask him to clarify that now so that we have a proper record of who's actually doing these things he's talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Dr. Simic, you heard what the Prosecution is asking for.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When I say "we," I am speaking on behalf of the organs of the municipal assembly and on behalf of a larger number of assemblymen in the municipal assembly, because there were others too who supported him.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the dislike between you and Stevan Todorovic deepened after everything that was done?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. He saw me as his greatest opponent. Especially he assumed that he would be left without the job of chief of police, and then he started resorting to different means in order to exert pressure upon me, starting with having me followed, spied on, and even -- I even suspect that he organised an assassination attempt against me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was this? In which period and in which way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There is a record about this shooting at my car. He organised this very quickly. And I would like to ask that this record be introduced by way of confirmation of my words, and this record was compiled by his service.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, what was the relationship between you and the volunteers who were in Samac, who were in the entourage of Stevan Todorovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For the most part, I did not have any contact with the volunteers. Some of them would very rarely stop by the premises of the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We are now going to move on to an analysis of two documents that were introduced previously.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Exhibit D58/3, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, just to -- by way of confirmation, you require D58/3?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Before we proceed to the document you are talking about, I would be interested in knowing what was the reason for the disagreement between Dr. Simic and Stevan Todorovic. Could you tell us a little bit about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You heard the question of His Honour Judge Lindholm. Could you please answer it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I told you that in 1990, when the first multi-party elections were held, I did not want Stevan Todorovic to be on the same list with me. But I'm not going to talk about his symptoms. Then I was against him being proposed by the assembly for any position, let alone chief of police.
