In the future also -- whenever I could, when I could prevent him from being present in any body, I always spoke against Stevan Todorovic being in such a body. When he was replaced in 1994, I was against having him given any leading position in the territory of the Municipality of Samac, because I thought that a personality with such structure does not know how to be in a leading position at all, and on the other hand, he would only disgrace all of us. That's what I thought. That's how I behaved. Hence, the animosity between the two of us. That is the genesis of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: If I may continue my questioning. How does it come that he, though, was a member of the Crisis Staff in 1972 [sic] and upwards, although you were resisting him all the time? Can you explain that to me. Because there's -- this has been told by different witnesses before this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The year written down here is 1972 in the transcript, and you probably meant 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] 1992, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We introduced the payrolls of the Crisis Staff, and I think that in this way we proved that Stevan Todorovic was not a member of the Crisis Staff and that he falsely represented himself here as a member of the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Did I hear your answer accurately? Forcibly, or in which way did he become a member of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that Stevan Todorovic was not a member of the Crisis Staff and that we proved this by exhibiting the payroll of the Crisis Staff from May 1992 two days ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, for Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Your microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Sorry. Sorry. If I may be of assistance to the inquiry of His Honour Judge Lindholm, Your Honour, you can find on page 46, line 18 an accurate translation of what Dr. Simic just said. The gist of it is that Mr. Stevan Todorovic falsely represented himself here, in the Tribunal before this Trial Chamber, as a member of the Crisis Staff. That was the right words that Dr. Simic used. Not forcibly, but falsely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Falsely. Okay. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: But how is that possible?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well, it's a dimension of the truth, actually, of versions of truth and, you know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: We have heard through many mouths that he was a member of the Crisis Staff, not only through the mouth of Stevan Todorovic. Can that be explained.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well, to some extent it can be. This is a Defence case, and we shall present appropriate evidence with regard to that issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And allow me to emphasise, Your Honour, that we heard that in category of hearsay of the Prosecution witnesses because they were not members of any official institutions. They were allegedly victims, and victims by itself. So they heard that maybe Stevan Todorovic was -- was a member of Crisis Staff. If you go and make an analysis of the witness statements. Only witness Stevan Todorovic here gave his explanation and some extended version of his point of view to that extent. And also, I would like to draw your attention, Your Honour, to the municipal Official Gazette number 1, where the members of executive boards -- board are, including Stevan Todorovic as the chief of police. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please take a look at this document. Could you tell me briefly whether you were familiarised with it at the time of its creation and what is this about and what was the basis for this conclusion. Excuse me. Let us clarify this, because the 23rd of November is the date in the English version. How do you interpret the date in the original, in the Serbian version that is right in front of you? And could you please put this Serbian version on the ELMO. Is it the 23rd of November or is it some other date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I read this as the 23rd of November, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please look at the top of this document now, when it refers to the session held on such and such a date. What is the date there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The 28th of November, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what do you infer on that basis?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The 28th of November, 1992 is more legible, as far as I'm concerned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what about the date at the bottom of the page? What could that be?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The 28th of November, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Just a small correction with regard to the translation, because in the English translation -- could you please -- Ms. Usher, could you please --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I think we've observed that already, so just go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So do you remember some discussion regarding this conclusion at the War Presidency?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the objective of adopting this conclusion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The objective was to, regardless of the wartime, summon all assemblymen and commence the work of the Municipal Assembly of Samac Municipality. And based on the instructions coming from the republic, to abolish the Crisis Staff, the War Presidency. And then finally on the 17th of December, the People's Assembly -- I think there was a decree coming from the republic level. I'm not sure from which organ specifically. This decree regulated the abolishment of War Presidencies, which means that regular municipal parliaments had to be convened irrespective of the war situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Usher. Could we have now Exhibit D60/3, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What was the objective of this decision and who prepared the draft of the decision?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This decision was prepared by the executive council of the Samac Municipal Assembly, and its purpose was to aid the civilian protection, place and manner of burying fallen Serb soldiers and those who had died.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In order to convey properly the meaning of this word in English, I'm not really happy with the translation. When you say "civilian protection," do you mean the organ that exists within the National Defence structure? Is that what you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Here during the proceedings, during the Prosecutor's case, several topics were raised, and I would like to ask you now whether you personally ever - of course before arriving to The Hague - were in contact with a certain document known as Variant A and B.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you familiarise yourself with the contents of that document here in The Hague, that document that we refer to here as Variant A and B?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the Crisis Staff or any other organ, according to your knowledge, have contact in Samac or have you heard from somebody else who knew of this document known as Variant A and B?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know about whether somebody in civilian or military organs discussed Variant A and B in Samac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, just for the record, I have to make certain references now to the -- to the witness statements that we heard here in order to have a proper way of examination. So I would like to make some references to certain witnesses that appeared here before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. You can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When the testimony of Mr. Sulejman Tihic is concerned, tell me please, were you ever a client of Sulejman Tihic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was an attorney in Samac, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were president of the municipal board of the SDS, and he was president of the municipal board of the SDA; therefore, could you tell us how often did you meet in the official capacity during late 1991 and up until April of 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was not the first president of the SDA in Samac. Izet Izetbegovic was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I limited that to the time period mentioned in the indictment, specifically from October of 1991 until April of 1992, so please tell me about that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We would meet each other at municipal assembly sessions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how often would that be?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: These sessions were held once a month, once every two months, and they were not held at all in the period immediately before the beginning of the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did you talk about on those occasions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't remember speaking to each other directly at all during that period.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any cooperation with him due to party work? Did you analyse material for assembly sessions? Did you work together in any party committees?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you just told us that you met with him at assembly sessions - that's what you've just told us - and in order to make sure that it is all logical, I'm asking you now in what capacity did you meet each other at those assembly sessions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As assemblymen of the Municipal Assembly of Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that occasion, would you normally greet each other? Would you exchange any words? Did you discuss the agenda of the session?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The municipal assembly has 50 assemblymen. Then there are members of the executive council and other professional staff members, so normally through there would be 50 to 60 people, and I don't think that I specifically exchanged any words with him or shook hands with him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the municipal board of SDS have any contacts with the municipal board of the SDA and HDZ?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: These contacts were carried out by clubs of MPs. There was a club of MPs of the SDS, that of the HDZ, and all other parties. So every party had its club of MPs in the municipal assembly that represented the interests of that party.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see Mr. Sulejman Tihic in private, privately, or did you meet with your families?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you sit with him in cafes or restaurants in Bosanski Samac prior to April of 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever talk to him about the future set-up of Yugoslavia or political problems and how they could be solved in that first trimester of 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not with him personally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who did you discuss it with, then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those were daily issues discussed among all citizens.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you on one occasion -- no. First of all, were you ever with him in a restaurant owned by Hamde Tobakovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On which occasion you said you would sacrifice your child for the future of the state.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have never stated that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you frequent the Cafe AS?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you frequent the pizzeria of the Bicic brothers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever say to Sulejman Tihic that Serbs were used to being in war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sulejman Tihic and I didn't know each other well enough in order to have any personal conversation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you this specifically because this is something that a witness stated here. So we will now go question by question. Have you ever told Sulejman Tihic that Serbs were used to wars?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just prior to the breakout of war in Bosanski Samac, a meeting was held between the municipal officials and those of political parties. Were you familiar with what went on on that meeting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Based on your recollection, when was this meeting held? What date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The 14th or 15th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At whose initiative was this meeting called?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the initiative of the president of the municipal board of the SDS for the Municipalities of Samac, Odzak, Gradacac, and Orasje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who attended the meeting, based on your recollection? You don't have to give us every single name, but those that you remember.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Representatives of all three parties from these four municipalities were present there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember any names?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: President of Gradacac municipality, Sefko Seric -- I think that's what he was called; president of municipal board of the SDS of Odzak, Dragomir Tesanovic then representatives of the SDA and HDZ from Odzak, whose names I don't know; then there was Cvijetin Josipovic from Orasje and representatives of the HDZ and SDA from Orasje; and then from Samac I think there were Mato Nujic, Filip Evic, Izet Izetbegovic, Mirko Jovanovic, and I. But it is possible that I made a mistake with respect to some of the names.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Sulejman Tihic present there at the meeting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't remember him being there at the meeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were the topics discussed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Lisbon Agreement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In what respect? What parts of it were discussed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the sense of implementing or discussing the implementation of the Lisbon Agreement on the ground. This envisaged the division into three cantons along the ethnic lines in one state where all decisions would be passed based on consensus and where that state was supposed to resemble Switzerland.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the position of those who were present? What were the viewpoints expressed, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The meeting was a constructive one, a calm one. Representatives of Odzak, Gradacac, and Orasje mostly agreed that these talks should be continued similar to the way they are conducted at the highest level, and it was agreed that we should meet the following Wednesday and then meet once a week. The Lisbon Agreement envisaged a possibility that set forth, that if the interested parties were unable to agree, on introducing an international arbitration that was to resolve disputes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were members of the military present at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mico Djurdjevic, a retired colonel, was present at the meeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were any other members of the military there at the meetings, in the corridors around the building? Were there any guards? Was there an increased number of soldiers there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, there were no other soldiers there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Colonel Djurdjevic say anything regarding this issue?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't think that he took part in discussion at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you mention some ultimatums or some deadlines by which the agreement had to be reached and some threats if there was a failure to reach such agreements?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Nobody mentioned any ultimatums or deadlines, nor was the -- nor did the Lisbon Agreement include any deadlines.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "nobody," you include yourself, don't you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's what I'm asking you. Did you with Sulejman Tihic from the SDA and Evic from HDZ go to do rounds of the barriers in the area on the eve of the conflict? So I'm talking about March and perhaps early April 1992.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We visited two villages, but it was on the day when the Muslims in Samac put up barricades to face Serb villages and when they prevented the Serb population from entering the town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you be more specific as to the date. When was it that you visited those?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was sometime in late 1991, early 1992. I wouldn't know the exact date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 17th of April, 1992 did you make a call to Boro Pisarevic and did you talk with Sulejman Tihic on that occasion and did you tell him on the same occasion that he should surrender and that there would be no negotiations with his side and that the Serbs would continue until the final victory?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever talk with Sulejman Tihic that day at all, on some other occasion but on that same day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Just for the sake of clarity, your question on line 25 of page 56, you -- where you've got a number of pieces in there. One of the questions would be: Did you make a call to Boro Pisarevic? Number two: Did you talk with Sulejman Tihic on that occasion? And then number three: Did you go on and talk about surrender? And we just have one answer: "No." Could we find out whether, first of all, there was a telephone call made by Dr. Simic to Mr. Pisarevic's home.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you answer that question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not make any calls that day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you talk with Simo Zaric and Sulejman Tihic a few days after the 17th of April when Sulejman Tihic was having an interview at Simo Zaric's, and did you say on that occasion that you were not responsible for his release?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: In relation to following up to Judge Williams's question, there were three questions asked in one. Mr. Pantelic has just put to the witness, or the accused, one of those. The two other questions still remain unanswered. It's unclear whether the "no" was referring to one, two, or three of those.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. In fact, I'm referring to certain portions of the previous testimonies of OTP witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. That is -- that is clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Of episodes, you know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And then in general I put that to the witness and he will say simply whether he's aware of that event or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. So do we take it that the "no" is --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Is for all the episodes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Is for all. Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you've understood what I've said. I'm telling you what some witnesses for the Prosecution said here. And after all, you heard them. You know very well which witnesses I'm referring to. In this specific case, I'm referring to Sulejman Tihic, who testified here and who spoke about certain episodes before this Chamber and his perception of your role in all this. So when I'm trying to arrive at some clarifications, you are giving me your affirmative or negative answers, but they refer to the entirety of the episodes that I present to you. Did you ever meet Sulejman Tihic in the restaurant which belonged to Hranaprodukt company, the occasion on which he was bloodied and bruised?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see Sulejman Tihic in the same condition elsewhere in Samac in April 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Pantelic, your question on page 58, line 24/25 and on to the following page wasn't answered. Did you talk with Simo Zaric and Sulejman Tihic a few days after the 17th when Sulejman Tihic was having an interview at Simo Zaric's, et cetera. So we need to get an answer whether he talked on that occasion. And secondly, when you say "an interview at Simo Zaric's," do you mean at his apartment? Do you mean at an office in the police station or wherever else?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: When I -- yeah, I will clarify that. When I said "interview," in official sense -- in Serbian language that means "informativni razgovor," which is very limited to the issue. So maybe it's a matter of translation, but I will clarify that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Yeah. But it does -- that still doesn't address the issue of the location at Simo Zaric's -- at Simo Zaric's. At which location? Home? Office?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right. So did you a few days after April the 17th talk with Simo Zaric and Sulejman Tihic by telephone when Sulejman Tihic was arrested and when he was taken for an interview at Simo Zaric's?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you say on that occasion to Simo Zaric that you were not -- that it was not in your jurisdiction to have Sulejman Tihic released?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you mean by this, that it was not in your jurisdiction?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I meant that it was up to the Ministry of the Interior exclusively.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, could I still have an answer as to at which location. Again, we're saying this time now that it was after Mr. Tihic was arrested and when he was taken for an interview at Simo Zaric's. Again, are we talking about the police station?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Well, you heard the question asked by Judge Williams. Did you talk with Mr. Simo Zaric while he was in the police station?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was answering questions concerning my telephone call. I am not sure where I was called from, but I think that that conversation took place, and hence my answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me. Sorry to belabour the point, but I think it's quite important to know whether after Mr. Tihic was arrested - and he was now being interviewed by Mr. Zaric- whether this was in an official location such as the SUP building and was not, shall we say, a more casual tete-a-tete in a cafe or somewhere else.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that occasion, when you had this conversation with Simo Zaric, when you talked over the telephone --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I was just informed by the client that they don't receive anything in their earphones, so they cannot follow the trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we have some assistance on the earphones.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you hear the interpretation now? [In English] They didn't hear your question, in fact, Your Honour, so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Oh, I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So that's maybe a matter of technical --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: If it can be repeated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Is it working now, Mr. Tadic, Mr. Zaric? Can you hear? You can hear? Okay. Well, maybe I'll just repeat the last question, not the series. I was wanting to know whether the conversation on the telephone between Dr. Simic and Mr. Tihic, when Mr. Tihic had been arrested and was being interviewed in Mr. Zaric's, according to the answer, whether that interview between Mr. Zaric and Mr. Tihic was in the SUP building or whether it was in some other location.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when you received that phone call, were you informed, did you know where Simo Zaric was calling you from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not sure that I asked him that or that I gave it a thought. The problem was that Sulejman Tihic had been arrested and that Simo Zaric and Sulejman Tihic were looking for the way to set him free, and I said that it was not within my terms of reference either to arrest him or to set him free.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: So I assume the answer is you don't know where this interview was going on. All you know is that Mr. Tihic had been arrested and he was with Mr. Zaric.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And during that telephone conversation that we are talking about, did you also talk personally by telephone with Mr. Sulejman Tihic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you repeat to him that position that you've just told us about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. In the restaurant which belonged to Hranaprodukt company, did you meet any of the witnesses for the Prosecution who had testified before this Chamber at the time when he was bloody and bruised?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. Nor am I aware that in the Hranaprodukt restaurant there was a soup kitchen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But did you see any of the witnesses for the Prosecution having testified before this Court who would be bloody and bruised anywhere else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you once talk with Simo Zaric about Dikan's murder, committed by Lugar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot recall that conversation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In relation to Dragan Lukac, do you know him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Only by sight.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know what his particular trade was, what was his occupation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you used to see him in the medical centre officially?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you present at the meeting held on the 6th of March, 1992 in the police station in Samac, the meeting at which -- no, let me ask you this first: Were you present at that meeting in the police station?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that occasion, at the meeting, was Colonel Nikolic there too, Captain Petrovic, a security officer; Vinko Dragicevic, from the police; then Milan Jekic, also from the police; and Mirko Lukic? Were they all present there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the subject matter discussed there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The implementation of the agreement signed by the Yugoslav People's Army and the Minister of the Interior, Alija Delimustafic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you comment on that agreement on that occasion and what was your position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not comment on it, and I took no position.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you attend a meeting held on the 12th of April, 1992 in the premises of a neighbourhood community, a meeting attended by you, Dragan Lukac, and Simo Zaric?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have no recollection of such a meeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that meeting you allegedly discussed certain activities of the army, and Lukac opposed it and you were, as he put it, indolent, with reference to those topics.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember attending that meeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Dragan Lukac at a meeting in the municipal hall on the 15th of April, 1992 that you mentioned a while ago, the meeting of municipalities and party officials, discussing the principles of the Lisbon Agreement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you order to arrest Dragan Lukac in Crkvina on the 17th of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you attend a meeting on the 11th of April, 1992 to discuss the appointment of Dragan Lukac as chief of police, as proposed by the HDZ?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With reference to Izet Izetbegovic, after the meeting in the municipal hall on the 15th of April, 1992 did you go together to a restaurant and -- no, first, did you go to a restaurant with him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you perhaps mention to him under some other circumstances that the Serbs would resort to force, to which he responded that you would end up as Dr. Mengele.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We never conducted any such harsh conversations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you about this.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I never said that. And Izet Izetbegovic is a person that I like very much, and I'm really fond of him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But did he tell you that you would end up as Dr. Mengele?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go with Izet Izetbegovic to the regional staff of the TO in Doboj towards the end of 1991 or beginning of 1992 in the capacity of municipality officials so that you would resolve the question of withdrawing weapons by the TO into JNA depots?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know Esad Dagovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your official capacity, did you enter the building of the Municipal Assembly of Samac in the period from April to August 1992? And how often, if so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that I did not go into it practically at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you present at a meeting in the village of Struke near Prud towards the end of March 1992 in the house of a certain Mr. Nijemcevic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that you should put shorter questions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Towards the end of March 1992 were you in the house of Mr. Nijemcevic in Struke on any occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you explain the occasion and could you explain other details related to your stay at that house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was a private house, a private visit attended by neighbours. My visit was a very short one. But I am convinced that the witness who talked about some meeting there was not present in the house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you come from when you came to this house in Struke? From which direction?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The direction of Samac. It is very close to Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long were you there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 15 to 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you go afterwards?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that I had to do a house-call. I think that I went to see a certain patient.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you perhaps remember - it's been ten years after all - but which time of day was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it was the morning hours. In the morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Blaz Paradzik present at the meeting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't think he was present.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go -- did you come by yourself or did you come with somebody else to that house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that I came by myself. I do not remember anybody else being with me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that occasion did you talk about a plan of annexing the villages where the majority population was Serb in the surroundings of Odzak; that is to say, the annexation of these villages to the municipality of Samac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You personally or the Crisis Staff, did you issue passes to civilians to leave town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know Alija Fitozovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: By sight.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In April 1992 or later, did you have any personal knowledge about the activities of Alija Fitozovic in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What was talked about in town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was talked about in town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That he established a unit consisting exclusively of Muslims, that he armed it, that he established various checkpoints, night-time checkpoints that were observing movements of the population, and it was basically within that framework.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am going to convey an episode to you now that Stevan Todorovic spoke about, and you are going to give me an answer as to whether that was an accurate description of this episode, or perhaps if you have some explanations, feel free to give them. On the 12th of April, 1992 were you present at the premises of the company of the Agro Posavina in Donji Zabar at a meeting that was attended by Colonel Nikolic as well, then Mico Ivanovic and Stevan Todorovic, and on that occasion Colonel Nikolic informed about the arrival of a group of volunteers from Serbia in the region of Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you present --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Let's just be clear -- clearer maybe.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The answer given is no. It means -- the accused means he was not present at that meeting; is that what it means? Or that the things suggested were not discussed? What is the correct interpretation?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You heard Judge Mumba.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That means that I was not present at the meeting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you present at a meeting on the 15th of April, 1992 in Obudovac that was attended by the following persons including yourself, that is Milos Bogdanovic, Savo Popovic, Dusan Tanasic, Mico Ivanovic, and Mirko Jovanovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that there were other names involved too. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were at that meeting.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us, what are the other names? What was it that you wanted to add? Who else was there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm already tired and it's hard for me to focus now.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: It's 1.00, Your Honour. Maybe we could have a break and then I have virtually - maximum 15 questions - 15 episodes like this and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic. Because sometimes you're going in too much detail, which is not necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay, Your Honour, I will take your instructions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So how long do you think you will take? Because you were supposed to take half an hour. You went on --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Let me say 15 minute, 20 maximum.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. 20 minutes when we start in the afternoon. We'll adjourn now and resume our proceedings at 14.30 hours. --- Luncheon recess taken at 1.00 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So Dr. Simic, before the break, we talked about this meeting on the 15th of April, 1992 in Obudovac. How far away is Obudovac from Samac and in which direction?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The microphones for the accused.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Around 20 kilometres, to the east, towards Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before the break you said that apart from those names that I mentioned, there were some other persons attending the meeting. Have you remembered in the meantime? Can you give us the other names?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From which direction did you come to Pelagicevo -- sorry, Obudovac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From the direction of Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that occasion did you say to those who were present that you were coming from Colonel Nikolic, who has provided information that over the next 48 hours, according to his information, there is going to be an attack by Croat and Muslim forces against Samac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you inform those present that members of the Crisis Staff who were proposed should be in Crkvina on the 16th of April in the evening hours?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you say then that Colonel Nikolic insisted that Fadil Topcagic should be on the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the topic on the agenda of that meeting, briefly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Information regarding the meeting in the Municipal Assembly of Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that occasion, did you say that Stevan Todorovic, Milos Bogdanovic, and you should be in Crkvina and that after that you should address the inhabitants of Samac after the military operation is over?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From April until the end of 1993 did Stevan Todorovic report to you personally orally about the situation and about the conditions of imprisonment in Bosanski Samac in which the prisoners were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You personally, or the Crisis Staff as an institution, did you give instructions to start investigation proceedings against Croats or Muslims who took part in the armed rebellion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that relates to you personally and to the Crisis Staff as an institution.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was in charge of these proceedings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the Crisis Staff have the authority to release larger groups of prisoners who were envisaged for an exchange procedure?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you personally have such authority?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Around the 19th of April, 1992 did you say over the telephone to Stevan Todorovic that Sulejman Tihic was in the apartment of Boro Pisarevic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Excuse me if I interrupt you, but going back to page 71 and line 11: Did the Crisis Staff have the authority to release larger groups of prisoners, and so on, and then going forward. Who had the authority?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You heard the question of Judge Lindholm.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Ministry of the Interior and Ministry of Justice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: And if I may continue, on which level -- or rather, of which level are we now talking?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In Samac, at the level of the municipality of Samac, which organ was in charge of the exchange procedure of a large number of prisoners?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Are we now speaking of the exchange or the imprisonment?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The exchange.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Both.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The exchange is a complex procedure, and it was under the control of the Ministry of Justice but also all security services in the field, both military and police.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As for the detention and imprisonment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Ministry of the Interior was in charge of those affairs, as was the military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: May I proceed, Your Honour, with the questions?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please tell me, did Stevan Todorovic have to ask for approval, a written or a verbal one, from the Crisis Staff if he wanted to release one of the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he have to ask for an approval from you personally?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you personally know that the prisoners in the first few weeks after the conflict broke out, between the 16th and 17th of April, were taken for their meals to the restaurant of the Uniglas factory?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I learned of it later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: During May of 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you remember who did you learn this from?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, maybe I'm --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I was listening very carefully to what the accused said, and I believe he said during November 1992, but I could be wrong, of course. Here it says "May."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we have that clarified. Was it may or --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: If I'm wrong, I do apologise to the witness and to the Trial Chamber also.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please tell us, when did you learn that prisoners were taken for their meals to the restaurant of the Uniglas factory?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I learned of it during May of 1992. And as to whom did I learn this from, after ten years I really can't tell you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Stevan Todorovic inform you personally about the establishment of detention units in such locations as the elementary school, secondary school, and the TO building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether he informed about this the institution itself? I mean the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He informed the Crisis Staff that there were prisoners.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you, as a member of the Crisis Staff, did you acquire that information at that time as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could you be more specific?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since in your previous answer you said that he did not inform you about this personally, and now you are telling us that the Crisis Staff as an institution was informed -- now, in view of the fact that you were the president of the Crisis Staff, could you please clarify whether you in your capacity as president of the Crisis Staff had information about these locations where people were imprisoned of which you were informed through Stevan Todorovic -- the Crisis Staff was informed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had that information which he presented at the sessions of the Crisis Staff, which were mostly quite limited and boiled down to the fact that there were some prisoners.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anybody speak about the conditions under which prisoners were kept? Did anybody speak about their treatment or possible measures to be taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Stevan Todorovic inform you that Lugar had killed Dikan?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you personally know about the fact that some members of the volunteer units were mistreating prisoners?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Stevan Todorovic inform you that he had killed the person nicknamed Antesa?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know that Father Jozo Puskaric was detained?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you personally decide who was eligible to be exchanged?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you personally have anything to do with work obligation in Odzak?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware of plunder, certain cases of plunder carried out by members of volunteer units, cases in which certain vehicles were stolen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I knew of it partially.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please explain this.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know. What do you mean, "explain this"?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you said that you partially knew of it, so my first question would be: What cases were you aware of?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the road one could see a volunteer driving a vehicle, and I would ask him where did he get that vehicle, and the driver would explain to me that he had taken the vehicle from somebody.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ask for an explanation from police organs? Did you take steps to have such cases prosecuted?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In principle, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Perhaps that could be clarified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: This is a very confusing answer. "In principle, yes." Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please be more precise.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I tried to ensure that all organs did their job, that the Ministry of the Interior did what it was supposed to, that the judiciary did this as well, and they were in charge of these matters. The police organs and the judiciary were in charge of this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: If I may continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: As to the action taken by the accused, it's not a sufficient answer to say "in principle." Did you or did you not?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I would like to add this: Did you request the police to instigate proceedings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, both from the police and the judiciary. I requested them to put an end to criminal acts and to prosecute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Dr. Simic, when you made these requests, were these verbal requests or were these requests in writing, signed by yourself on behalf of the Crisis Staff, War Presidency, whatever?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Those were verbal requests and practical moves, steps. So verbal requests to have this done and practical steps to ensure logistics necessary, both to the Ministry of the Interior and the judiciary to carry out their duties. One of the practical steps taken was that we designated a coordinator who was in charge of coordinating the judicial organs in our municipality. Then we also asked the Ministry of the Interior to demobilise those judges who were at the front so that they could come back and do their work.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Your Honours, before Mr. Pantelic goes on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The witness -- sorry, Dr. Simic again used the word "we" in his last answer. Again, I seek clarification of what we means. We is more than one person. Does he mean we the Crisis Staff, we the assembly, we, myself and one other person?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Can we have clarification, please, from the accused.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And I stress that I seek it every time the word "we" is used, that it's clarified exactly who Dr. Simic is talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think that it is in the interests of your case to be more precise.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I say "we," that pertains either to the Crisis Staff or to the War Presidency or to the municipal parliament.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Well, that's not the clarification that I'm seeking with respect. The clarification -- there are three different organs Dr. Simic is talking about there. He's just saying it would be one of the three. In my submission, we should know exactly which one he's referring to every time he does and that he doesn't use the word "we" without explaining what he means by "we."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. And this last question, when he's talking about asking the Ministry of the Interior to demobilise the judges who were at the front so they could come back and do their work. He did say "we." At that stage, which institution is he referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have heard the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, it wasn't translated well. I said that we requested the Ministry of Defence, not the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But the key point here is who do you mean by "we"? Please be very specific. Do you mean I, Dr. Simic? Do you mean the Crisis Staff as an institution or the War Presidency as the institution? This is the essence that we need to gather from your answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I tried to never speak on behalf of myself personally. I was president of the municipal assembly while the Crisis Staff existed. It existed in lieu of the municipal assembly. The War Presidency also existed in lieu of the municipal assembly. And then the municipal assembly itself started functioning, and I always was a representative of that body. And when I say "we," I refer to that body, depending on which time period the question pertained.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Precisely, that is the reason why we also want specifications, because it seems at different periods different institutions were operating or in charge.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, precisely so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We are now discussing the fact that you saw some volunteers driving vehicles that they appropriated. In what period of time did you observe this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Between May and June of 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you then take the steps that you mentioned in terms of putting requests that some legal measures be taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Measures were taken by the Crisis Staff in a sense that they wanted to prevent crime in the territory of our municipality by requesting competent organs to do their job.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that the goods from the furniture factory were transferred to a town called Ruma in Serbia throughout 1992 and 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you give us more details. What was the time period and what were the reasons for transferring these goods?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There's a decree of the government of Republika Srpska to put on the market final goods and to take out the goods from the war zone so that they can be used later on or bartered for other goods.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was in charge of that in Samac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The executive council, Secretariat for Economy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you know, please tell us what kind of a company, in terms of property ownership, was the furniture factory? Was it public, private, or state-owned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was state-owned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was in charge of managing and leading that factory, if it was state-owned indeed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Ministry of Economy of Republika Srpska was in charge of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge whether Stevan Todorovic travelled to Belgrade in the summer of 1992 in order to intercede on behalf of Crni and have him released from detention?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you advise or prompt practically Milos Bogdanovic in relation to a number of people who were to be sent to Serbia for training?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you, together with Miroslav Tadic and Simo Zaric, make plans concerning the persecution of non-Serb population in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you make such plans with some other people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you, Miroslav Tadic, and Simo Zaric plan or in any other way aided, abetted, or organised the deportation in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not understand that word. What does "deportation" mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you, Simo Zaric, and Miroslav Tadic plan, carry out, or organise in some other way forcible transfer of non-Serb population or ethnic cleansing from Samac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't understand the term "ethnic cleansing" either. I need a precise question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I've finished with my examination-in-chief, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Your Honours, before Mr. Pantelic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: But can you explain to the witness your question, because he hasn't answered, because he complained that he doesn't understand "ethnic cleansing" either. Can you use simple terms in your question so that he can understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Did you, Simo Zaric, and Miroslav Tadic prepare, plan, or organise in some other way the procedure of exchange of the civilian population to and from Samac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot answer yes or no to that question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, then can you give us a broader answer? What kind of an answer can you give us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can say that we did not plan any departure of the non-Serb population from the territory of the Samac municipality, nor was it ever our objective.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you personally have a discriminatory attitude towards the non-Serb population in Bosanski Samac, in terms of their ethnic or religious background, of the non-Serb population?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I think I've finished, Your Honour, my examination-in-chief. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Your Honours, before Mr. Pantelic sits down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The Prosecution -- it appears he hasn't put to his client the allegations contained in paragraphs 11 and 12 of the indictment. That's the wider context of Bosnia. He appears to have confined his last questions to Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Although it is the choice of the Defence how they put it, but it's fair to the accused to put things to him which are in the indictment so that he has an opportunity to deal with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well, it -- for us as a Defence we think that there is not any evidence with regard to that issue, but I would of course follow the suggestion and instructions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Therefore, did you, Miroslav Tadic, and Simo Zaric plan the process of banishment of the non-Serb population in a broader area of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I had indicated earlier that you can finish your questions as planned. But in view of the matters that were raised by the Prosecution yesterday, we shall not formally close the examination-in-chief. We'll wait and see whether there will be any further developments which may necessitate your putting some more questions to the accused.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Well, all three Defence teams were informed yesterday during the lunch break that pursuant to Rule 68, the Prosecution, I would say, has not fulfilled its obligations of disclosure of materials which may be possibly exculpatory for our clients. In particular, I was informed by the Prosecution that they recently discovered seven binders of such materials. Of course in relation to Rule 70, they have to, I would say, additionally make an overview and check of these materials, and then they will be in a situation to provide the Defence with the certain materials. Well, since this is an extremely serious issue, where in particular the Defence for Mr. Blagoje Simic was informed of that fact in the middle of examination-in-chief in capacity -- Dr. Simic in capacity of a witness before this Trial Chamber, I have accordingly informed my client yesterday and very briefly this morning about the legal aspects of that issue and problem. And since we are now in some kind of very hypothetical situation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Because that's what I was about to say, that --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: That is correct. Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The documents haven't yet been furnished to the Defence. Neither yourself nor your colleagues know to what extent, yeah, your cases may be affected. Perhaps we can wait for submissions until that is done, and I may as well go back to the Prosecution and find out the latest.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. And then maybe we could be in a situation to respond and to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yeah, of course, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Of course. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Maybe the accused can move back to the former seat. If I may explain to the accused, you are still continuing with the examination-in-chief. The finalisation will be dealt with later of the procedural issues have been discussed by the Trial Chamber and the parties. But in the meantime, since you're not giving evidence any more, you may go back to your former seat. Yes, the Prosecution, any latest information after what you submitted yesterday?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I can inform the Trial Chamber the situation is the following: Mr. Pantelic just referred to seven binders. There may be some confusion there. The seven binders are binders of material in relation to Dr. Blagoje Simic only as a result of a system-wide name search in relation to him. The Prosecution received that material, I think it was late on Monday night, and we are in the process of reviewing those seven binders at the moment. We are reviewing it obviously for, one, our own purposes, and two, to comply with Rule 68, which is to disclose to the Defence the existence of material known to the Prosecutor. We are presently going through those seven binders. In relation to the two remaining defendants, those searches should be completed, I'm told, by the close of business on Tuesday. That is only in relation to their names, a system-wide or an all-system search in relation to their names. The Prosecution hopes to be able to complete its review of that material for the purposes of Rule 68 by the end of next week. That is only in relation to the names of the defendant -- of the three accused. So it's not a matter of turning over seven binders.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, no. Yes, that is appreciated. But I seem to be confused. You are indicating that you'll be able to complete reviewing the material concerning Dr. Blagoje Simic when?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I can't give you -- unfortunately I cannot give you a precise date. The mechanics of this -- the material comes from many different collections that the OTP holds in its evidence and information support unit, millions of documents. His name is entered into the system and it comes -- the name may come up in many, many, different contexts, including in testimony in this case and in witness statements, which the accused -- the Defence of course already has. A lawyer has to go through and initially review all the material to find out, A, whether it's relevant, and B, whether it's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well. We don't need the details. So you are saying that you as Prosecution in this case may be able to complete your exercise by Tuesday?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: No. There are two issues. One is Dr. Simic. We are reviewing those seven binders at the moment. I can't tell you at the moment because -- this is why the mechanics are important. We need a --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Language translator to look at all the documents that are in B/C/S -- for obviously both sides. We will have the results of the searches of Mr. Tadic and Mr. Zaric by close of business Tuesday. We will then start to review those. They're one set of searches. In regard -- in relation to the witness searches I briefly spoke about yesterday, the Prosecution did all systems -- or system-wide searches on all the witnesses it called and provided that information as those witnesses were called during the course of the trial. Those haven't been updated, but that is not an enormous issue. They will be updated because obligation to disclose is obviously an ongoing one. The more important issue is the system-wide or all-systems search of the relevant criteria in relation to the defendants and all the other possibilities in the case. The estimate - and this is before we have all the search criteria and keywords. And we're working with the Defence, we have given them copies of the search in 1998, which was before another - I think - 3 million documents were added to the collection. They are providing us with their own keywords, which we will put into the system, which will hopefully shorten the proceedings. We don't know yet at the moment -- the estimate, as of yesterday -- that's without that specific information -- is maybe 100 person days. Now, person days is a term used for one person sitting, producing, and reviewing the material. It may produce 100 binders; it may not. We don't know. So the acting Prosecutor has -- is putting a team into place to start reviewing this material as soon as we have the results of it. Then we can start looking at it, and for the purposes of disclosure to the Defence. So I -- at this moment I cannot give any estimate of how long it will take. It could take -- it could take several months to do it. It could be shorter, depending upon what's produced and how many people we can get on to the job, because we need lawyers and translators who can sit down and look at every document which is produced.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Having received this information, the Trial Chamber will adjourn for half an hour and come back and inform the parties what the next course of action will be. But before we adjourn, we have a decision concerning the complaint that the Defence raised on the -- on Tuesday, the 12th of November, concerning the publication of the report of the expert witness, Professor Kecmanovic by a Sarajevo newspaper, namely the Dani magazine, on 3rd October, 2002 and for the refusal of the said newspaper to accede to the Defence requests to stop further publications. The Trial Chamber has found that the expert report of Professor Kecmanovic was publicly filed on 20th September. It was therefore available in the public domain. The Tribunal's practice is to public all public documents in all trials unless otherwise ordered by the Chamber. The suggestion, therefore, that the report may have been leaked from the Tribunal is clearly misconceived. The Trial Chamber would take action where appropriate if non-public material were disclosed to the public in violation of the Tribunal's rules and orders. In this complaint, the Trial Chamber finds that there was no legal impediment to the publication of the said report by the said newspaper, even before Professor Kecmanovic formally presented his report before the Trial Chamber, so no action can be taken by the Trial Chamber against the newspaper. We'll adjourn now and reconvene at 15.45.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I do apologise. On the previous issue, do we have a possibility to address the Trial Chamber on the issue that was just raised by the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. That's why we are coming back.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. Before -- I apologise. I've --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I really apologise for this. There's something I have to add. Can you just excuse me for one moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The -- in case there is any misapprehension about what I am saying on behalf of the Prosecutor to the Trial Chamber, it's not that we have failed to disclose. It's that we are in the process of reviewing. We have disclosed as we have gone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: That is understood. That has been understood. Your explanation has been understood.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you. I just want to make it completely clear that we understand the ongoing nature of the obligation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And this is something we're doing now, which we did before. We are updating an earlier search at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We've understood that, because we know that there is no limitation on Rule 68.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: It's an ongoing obligation. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: That is understood. We'll adjourn for half an hour. --- Break taken at 3.20 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The Defence wanted to say something, but it will be very, very brief because nothing has been discovered yet. Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well, just in principle, Your Honour, I would like to inform the Trial Chamber that yesterday I have discussed that matter, as I stated, with my client. And since this issue might affect very seriously his position and his defence -- I mean, speaking hypothetically, because my understanding was that a certain, I would say -- a quantity or number of documents which is now in a procedure for reviewing by the Prosecution, in terms of Rule 68, might be hypothetically of certain importance, firstly, for his testimony in chief here before the Trial Chamber. And then also with regard to the numerous lines of cross-examinations of various OTP witnesses in the Prosecutor case. So simply we are not in a situation to realise now without more details --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. That's why I said --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: From the Prosecution --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yeah. That's why I said briefly, because I know you haven't got the documents yet, if any.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: That's correct. Maybe my colleagues also have to add something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I wish to express my deep concern, having heard this information. Why, we are all familiar with Rule 68, and that the Prosecution is under permanent obligation. I shall remind you that at the Pre-Trial Conference when Catharine B. asked a question, my learned friend Di Fazio said quite clearly that he had disclosed all the material under Rule 68, that there was no other evidence. And now we hear that the Prosecution has been in possession of this material since 1998 and that they have been examining this material all the time. And I heard the Chamber voice its concern, not to mention us, twice already during the Prosecution case documents surfaced, the document for Esad Dagovic and Witness M, who turned up during the cross-examination. It is really a matter of utmost concern to us to learn the Prosecution has been in possession of this material for a long time and they have been systematising them through some database or what. The Defence is not interested how the Prosecution classifies its information, what it does. What we would like to know: If the Prosecution had this material during their case and they were aware of it, they had to disclose these documents to us straight away, if there are any said documents. And again, hypothetically, if the Prosecution comes across such documents and discloses them to us, we shall insist to learn when did the Prosecution come by that particular document which they are disclosing to us at this stage. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pisarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'm not going to repeat what my colleagues have already said. Merely, I wish to voice my profound concern with regard to the situation that we now find ourselves in. I think in view of the position of Mr. Zaric's defence, and it is identical with the position of Mr. Miroslav Tadic's defence, I will not be repeating what my colleague Mr. Lukic has said regarding the obligation of the Prosecution to, as we have a reciprocal procedure, and that they were simply duty-bound to immediately disclose the material to us immediately after having received this material. It is very important for us to obtain this information. We cannot say what we shall find in these new documents. But in any event, I think that without it, the participation in these proceedings will be brought into question, or rather, what would be brought into question would be adequate legal assistance to our client's, the accused, in this case. That is all. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I respond to something which Mr. Lukic said which is quite inaccurate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: In relation to the Prosecution's case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The Prosecution does not, as Mr. Lukic said -- has not had all this material in its possession and been reviewing it and withholding it in any way. The Prosecution has since 1998 added several million documents to its collection. They were not electronically searchable across the entire system until various stages of last year. The situation is we are aware of our ongoing obligation. We have to do another search of what is there. We do not know what is there and won't until we have the results and have reviewed it. We are not withholding any information. We are completely aware of the ongoing disclosure obligations. Now that we have become aware that we haven't done another systems search, we are doing one immediately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well. The Trial Chamber expects the Prosecution to work throughout the weekend and perhaps Monday and Tuesday to complete whatever they are doing about this, and the proceedings will continue on Wednesday. On Wednesday, we shall sit at 9.00 hours, which is 20th November. The accused should be ready for cross-examination on Wednesday, depending on the situation of the procedural matters that have been raised. So we'll adjourn until Wednesday, 20th November, at 9.00 hours.
